newsitem.title: FRANCE: Key facts about Algeria referendum voting.
newsitem.headline: Key facts about Algeria referendum voting.

text.p: Millions of Algerians are eligible to vote on a draft constitution on Thursday banning Moslem fundamentalists from seeking power in the North African country.
Here are details on the referendum:
ELECTORATE - There are 16.43 million people eligible to vote in Algeria, where voting is not compulsory. For the new constitution to come into force, 50 percent plus one of votes cast must be "Yes".
More than 217,000 young voters will be voting for the first time, having reached the mandatory minimum age of 18 years.
POLLING STATIONS - There are 35,533 polling stations in the country's 48 regions staffed by 380,000 election workers.
OPENING TIMES - Polling stations open at 8 a.m. (0700 GMT) and close at 8 p.m. (1900 GMT). The election law enables local authorities to change the times to accommodate voters.
Expatriate voters, numbering 735,034, began voting on Saturday.

Army and security forces voted on Monday to be ready to protect voters against Moslem guerrillas who threatened to disrupt poll. Bedouins, scattered in remote areas in the south, started voting on Monday.

TURNOUT - The authorities are hoping for a high turnout to give the government more legitimacy. Opposition leaders, who urged voters to boycott or cast "No" ballots, are hoping for a low turnout to embarrass the government.
Partial turnout figures will be released every few hours, most likely from midday.
COUNTING PROCEDURE - Local election officials will count votes at polling stations and pass them to the interior ministry headquarters for official release.

The government set up an independent election commission for last year's presidential election after opposition leaders insisted they must be able to oversee the polling process. But this time, the authorities said there was no need for such a body as there were enough legal guarantees to ensure a fair poll. The law entitles voters to watch the whole voting process.

VOTING PROCEDURE - Voters will be given an envelope and two pieces of paper: a white "Yes" one and a black "No" one. Every voter will then go into a private booth, insert one of the papers into the envelope before dropping his vote in the ballot box.
